result.caveats: Heavy white cloud cover over the southern half of the Island of Hawaii obscures the vent-to-plume connection; single RGB frame without SO2/aerosol optical depth product cannot definitively separate thin cirrus/humidity from vog; wind direction not independently verified.
evidence: Orange-red thermal hotspot pixels over east-central Island of Hawaii consistent with Kilauea location
Diffuse translucent blue-gray veil over ocean to east and southeast-south of Hawaii Island distinct from bright white opaque clouds and deep-blue clear ocean
Haze is anchored to/broadly emanating from Hawaii Island rather than entering as long-range transported layer from outside domain
No dense brown/gray wildfire smoke plume or distant source region visible
result.haze_description: Broad thin diffuse blue-gray veil over ocean east to southeast and south of the Island of Hawaii, partly under/mixed with bright white low clouds covering the southern half of the island; not a sparse black-background mask, no opaque dense plume, appearance is translucent vog haze.
result.image_type: true-color daytime visible satellite imagery showing islands, ocean and clouds, not a sparse black-background haze mask
